description: Hey everyone! We are a team of high school geniuses. Book your next trip to Mars with us! We are also very multilingual. We are fantastic (I'm so freaking sorry).
summary: We made an interactive, JavaScript-based game to get pre-teens and older interested in space missions and to learn about what it is like to be an astronaut. Through engaging gameplay design, children in K-12 could learn about the reality of being an astronaut on a mission.
details:
We built an educational game in JavaScript on Code.org that introduces children ages 7 to 12 to the realities of space missions.

The player begins with astronaut training on Earth, including underwater zero-gravity exercises, before launching to Mars. On the surface, they collect rock samples and learn about Martian geology. They then deploy MEDAs (Mars Environmental Dynamics Analyzers) and see how scientists use the data these instruments collect to understand Martian weather. Once the work is complete, the player returns to the spaceship and heads home to Earth.

Throughout the Mars missions, players must manage two survival meters. If oxygen drops too low or radiation climbs too high, the mission fails. This reflects the real constraints astronauts face and encourages careful planning.

By making space science interactive, the game helps children remember what they learn and builds early interest in astronomy. Inspiring more young people to pursue this field means more future astronomers and, ultimately, bigger discoveries.
